component: P16 fixed defensive mutation evidence and scoped module restoration
constraints: Four named trusted local source substitutions and four selected unittest methods; no automatic mutation discovery, arbitrary uploaded code or concurrent execution.
Compile captured source in a temporary module, require a successful complete unmodified baseline, restore two replaced bindings, reject visible listed-source changes.
alternatives: Direct Python compile/exec and scoped unittest.mock patch contexts.
mutmut automatic Python mutation discovery with fork/forkserver isolation.
Java/JVM PIT mutation testing for a JVM implementation.
Separate Python process for each selected mutation, supervised by Python, Node or Java.
rationale: KEEP direct Python mutation execution for the exact four source substitutions and actual tests under review. No cross-language source or semantic adapter is necessary.

mutmut provides broader discovery and POSIX process isolation; neither is the declared experiment. PIT would mutate JVM code rather than these Python function bodies. Neither supplies a demonstrated material advantage for this fixed diagnostic.

Per-experiment processes are appropriate if independent global-state isolation becomes required. Here trusted sequential tests restore two explicit bindings, with RuntimeError and KeyboardInterrupt controls; no sandbox or full-side-effect restoration is claimed.

Fresh live execution passes four baseline methods and observes eight assertion failures across four selected mutations. Removing source-change rejection in memory causes five existing regression assertions to fail. No new runtime or evidence mismatch demonstrated.
limits: The four substitutions are not a comprehensive mutation score, proof of causal completeness or cryptographic validation.
Captured source is compiled, but imported helpers/tests and unlisted dependencies are not attested. Before/after checks are not atomic.
Bounded experiment count does not impose a runtime deadline on arbitrary tests; this is trusted developer tooling, not a process supervisor.
Alternative tools were researched, not benchmarked. No migration winner is deferred; no choice rests on installed tooling, familiarity or rewrite cost.
